headline: Anthropic listed at a $1.3T market cap, and Europe's early-stage money went to AI tooling for chips, robots and space.
context_note: W47 was Slush week, so no comparison with previous weeks.

block1.title: Anthropic goes public

facts.text: priced at $83 a share, above the range. About $81.3bn raised, the largest IPO on record.

sources.quote: PRICES ITS UPSIZED IPO AT $83 PER SHARE, ABOVE THE $70-$78 MARKETED RANGE, RAISING $81.3B IN THE LARGEST OFFERING ON RECORD

facts.text: opened at $111.50 (+34%), closed at $97.17 (+17%). Market cap about $1.3T.

sources.quote: CLOSES UP 17% AT $97.17 IN ITS NASDAQ DEBUT, GIVING IT A MARKET CAP OF $1.3T
OPENING AT $111.50, UP 34% FROM ITS IPO PRICE

facts.text: AI sell-off. Asian tech fell: SoftBank about −15%, TSMC −5%+, Samsung and SK Hynix −6%+. The greenshoe took total proceeds to $93.5bn.

sources.quote: SOFTBANK FALLS ~15%, TSMC FALLS 5%+, AND SAMSUNG AND SK HYNIX FALL 6%+
BRINGING THE TOTAL RAISED IN ITS IPO TO $93.5B

block1.for_us: public investors have now priced a frontier lab. Late-stage AI marks get a public comparable, and early-stage pricing does not.

block5.text: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra: API tokens 20% cheaper than GPT-6 Astra, at $8 / $40 per million input/output tokens (Techmeme, AlphaSignal, 18 Nov). OpenAI also claims under one-third of GPT-6 Astra's cost per task on work and science evals. Google's Gemini 4 Neon: $3 / $15 per million input/output tokens. Inference got cheaper again, which helps application startups and squeezes resellers.
